quote_text:
Jimmy, talk us through your emotions  at the full-time whistle on that. 
Of course, it was a lot of frustration. I think  about how the game went and how the game was. 
Of course, you feel like you lose a game when  this happens in the last second of the game. 
So, of course, it was difficult. But we  also talk about it—we have to, some way,  
find a way to quickly move on now, and  we have an important game on Saturday.
We have some learning points from this game, I  think. The first half was really good. It was  
clear what we wanted to do—how we attacked the  box, how we run, run, opened space for each other.
The second half, when they played so low and were  waiting for transitions, we got more time on the  
ball. We got passive, and we started playing  each other instead of keeping attacking the box.
And that’s the worst thing you can do  in these kinds of games when the players  
are low and just waiting for transition—you  have to attack them much more and go for 3-1,  
instead of unconsciously  thinking about defending 2-1.
It can happen sometimes, but we get  a learning point from this today. And  
it’s difficult to explain why it happened.  It can happen—it’s happened in the past,  
it can happen in the future.  But we have to do much better.
And that’s why it’s so important to have  an identity—how we want to play the games  
against certain kinds of defences. So, of course it was tough. Still,  
we created quite good chances in the second half  even if you don’t attack as much as you want. 
But you know, the opponent always gets  one chance usually. Sometimes they score,  
sometimes they don’t—but today, they did. So... now we have to focus on the next thing.
Is that a game that you should win,  from 2–0 up against 10 men at half-time? 
Of course—you know that, and everybody knows that.  That’s why there’s frustration when you don’t. 
Also the way, maybe, the score  came—and this last second of the game.
But it’s up to us to improve and do  better next time it happens—be more  
aggressive in attack and keep attacking. Don’t give them so much time to reorganize  
or wait for the transition moments. Instead, be stronger—because when we  
put the ball into the box today, we  created, I think, two or three really  
strong chances in the second half also. So  that’s why we should do it more consistently.
You made four substitutions in about a five- or  six-minute period. If you'd seen the game out 2–1,  
I wouldn’t be talking about it. But do  you think that kind of helped change  
the impetus? Because I saw you quite  frustrated on the sideline, just urging  
the players to be quicker with their passing. Yeah, we had some players who were quite tired,  
and that’s why we got so low in some parts. Especially after their goal—the first goal  
they scored—I think we were in  the moment, and we should come on.
It’s a long time—we have to keep attacking, and we  tried to change the momentum there and do better.
It’s difficult to say right now why things happen  sometimes, because it was not a specific player. 
It was not our identity, not our game plan. It  can happen sometimes—when you get more time on  
the ball, instead of taking initiative, you send  the ball to someone else to take the initiative,  
instead of taking it yourself. We’ve talked  sometimes about starts for Aberdeen—you didn’t  
have that last weekend. This first half,  if you can take that into the semi-final,  
that’s going to be a big bonus.  And it’s a huge, huge match. 
It’s easy to forget everything when you lose that  goal today—that everything is bad. But it’s not.
There are still a lot of good things.  The result was not good for us today,  
but the performance in the first half—some parts,  how we created some chances in the second half— 
then, of course, we have to  do better in other parts also.
When we allowed the transitions  today—we have to be more... 
when we have, next time if it happens,  11 versus 10, we can’t be so passive.
Everybody knows—we’ll talk about it now.  And the best thing we can do right now— 
of course, we feel some frustration  tonight, we all do. Everybody who was  
here supporting, the atmosphere again,  it’s amazing in Aberdeen Football Club.
But we also have a really  important game on Saturday.  
So we have to just recover now  and focus on the right things.
Yeah, I think a lot of big  games still in the season,  
but now your focus is only on that one. Yeah, and then we have to go to the league again.
So right now all our focus is on the  semi-final in terms of the cup stage.
That’s probably bigger? I think in both parts we want to—if we want to be  
as we imagine ourselves in the future, what we’re  working for, it’s to cope in all competitions.
And that’s why we need a strong  squad and a strong mentality.
So for us it’s not going to be “this  or that.” We have to go for both.  
We’re still in two competitions,  and we want to do well in both.
Thank you. Thank you.
title: Jimmy Thelin FULL Post Match Press Conference | Aberdeen 2-2 Rangers
